name: Paris
vibe: Omid + Annika + Parents. Staying with family, some commitments. You've done the big sights. ~2.5 usable days. Parents love scenic beauty, markets, architecture, and food culture.

weather.conditions: Warm and mostly sunny, occasional afternoon thunderstorms

specialNotes.title: Breakfast Spots
specialNotes.body: Some mornings with family, some mornings out. Any neighborhood boulangerie will have excellent croissants and pain au chocolat. For a proper sit-down: Café de Flore (already on the list — order a croque monsieur and café crème), or Ob-La-Di in the Marais (specialty coffee + avocado toast + pastries, locals' favorite morning spot).

activities.name: Musée Carnavalet
activities.description: Le Marais, 23 Rue Madame de Sevigne. Museum of Paris history in two Renaissance mansions. Proust's cork-lined bedroom is here. Free, no reservation needed. Open Tue-Sun 10am-6pm. Parents will love this.

activities.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
activities.description: Tuileries. Monet's Water Lilies in purpose-built oval rooms. Intimate, ~1 hour.

activities.name: Musee de la Chasse et de la Nature
activities.description: Marais, 62 Rue des Archives. One of Paris's most unexpected museums. 17th-century mansions mixing historical art with contemporary interventions. Carved paneling, tapestries, witty curation. Completely off the tourist circuit. ~$15. Open Tue-Sun.

activities.name: Palais Royal garden
activities.description: Hidden in plain sight north of the Louvre. 17th-century enclosed arcaded square, Buren striped columns, chestnut trees. Most tourists walk past it.

activities.name: Marché d'Aligre
activities.description: Place d'Aligre, 12th. Paris's most authentic food market. Outdoor produce stalls + covered Beauvau hall for cheese, charcuterie, specialty foods. Tue-Sun mornings. Parents will love this.

activities.name: Coulée Verte / Promenade Plantée
activities.description: 12th, starts at Bastille. The elevated park on a former railway viaduct that inspired NYC's High Line. 4.7km walk, rose gardens, rooftop views. Below: artisan workshops (ceramicists, luthiers). Pairs naturally with Marché d'Aligre.

activities.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
activities.description: Marais, 39 Rue de Bretagne. Paris's oldest covered market (1615). The food stalls at lunch are the draw: Moroccan tagines, Japanese bento, Lebanese plates. Communal tables. Closed Mondays.

activities.name: Canal Saint-Martin to Belleville
activities.description: Iron footbridges, tree-lined quays, locks, then into Belleville's street art and multicultural food scene. Édith Piaf's neighborhood.

restaurants.name: Bouillon Julien
restaurants.vibe: 1906 Art Nouveau room — ornate mirrors, stained glass, plasterwork. Classic French comfort food at honest prices. Parents will gasp at the room.

restaurants.name: Bistrot Paul Bert
restaurants.vibe: Platonic ideal of a Paris bistro. Steak frites, souffle, tarte Tatin. Great wine list. Michelin listed.
restaurants.bookHow: +33 1 43 72 24 01 (hard to reach). Walk-in: arrive 7:30pm for patio.

restaurants.name: Le Servan
restaurants.vibe: Sisters Tatiana & Katia Levha. French bistro technique with Filipino-Asian soul. Period frescoes. One of Paris's most talked-about rooms.
restaurants.bookHow: Essential. Closed Sundays. Saturday dinner available.

restaurants.name: Le Café de l'Usine
restaurants.vibe: Time Out Paris recommended. Worker-priced lunch, precise rustic cooking. A real locals' room.

restaurants.name: Frenchie Bar à Vins
restaurants.vibe: Same kitchen as starred Frenchie next door, but walk-in. Small plates, great natural wine.

restaurants.name: Verjus Wine Bar
restaurants.vibe: Next to Palais Royal garden. American-owned, farm-to-table. Walk-in bar downstairs.

restaurants.name: Bistrot des Tournelles
restaurants.vibe: Newer Marais spot that feels decades old. Old-fashioned bistro charm, strong natural wine.

restaurants.name: L'As du Fallafel
restaurants.vibe: Most famous falafel in Paris. Jewish quarter, Le Marais. Cash only, always a queue.

restaurants.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
restaurants.vibe: Paris's oldest covered market (1615). Moroccan tagines, Japanese bento, Lebanese plates at communal tables. Lunch only.

restaurants.name: Septime
restaurants.vibe: Modern French, seasonal. The room feels like a cool pub, not stiff. Lunch (~$95) is a better entry point than dinner (~$155).

restaurants.name: Frenchie
restaurants.vibe: Global-inflected prix-fixe. The whole Rue du Nil block is a mini food destination.

bars.name: Candelaria
bars.vibe: 52 Rue de Saintonge, 3rd. Taqueria at front, unmarked door to one of Paris's best cocktail bars in back. World's Best Bars extended list.

bars.name: Bar Hemingway (Ritz)
bars.vibe: 15 Place Vendôme. 25 plush seats. Hemingway "liberated" this bar in 1944. $28-40/cocktail. Go for one drink. Parents will love the history.

bars.name: Harry's New York Bar
bars.vibe: 5 Rue Daunou, 2nd. Since 1911. Claimed birthplace of the Bloody Mary and French 75. 115 years of patina.

bars.name: La Buvette
bars.vibe: 67 Rue Saint-Maur, 11th. Iconic tiny natural wine bar in a former crémerie. Candlelit, cult vignerons, charcuterie on a mirror. Arrive early for a seat.

bars.name: Clown Bar
bars.vibe: 114 Rue Amelot, 11th. Next to Cirque d'Hiver. 1920s Art Nouveau tiles (listed historical monument). One of France's largest natural wine selections. Serious food too.

bars.name: Aux Deux Amis
bars.vibe: 45 Rue Oberkampf, 11th. Classic zinc bar, Art Deco, natural small-producer wines. Loud, busy, completely Paris.
